+def _outline_schema(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The stage-1 structured-output schema. ``layout_id`` is a closed ``enum`` built from
+    the manifest's own layouts -- an invented layout is rejected by the provider's own
+    structured-output mechanism, before it ever reaches ``validate_against_manifest``.
+    """
+    layout_ids = sorted({
+        lay["layout_id"]
+        for master in manifest.get("masters", [])
+        for lay in master.get("layouts", [])
+    })
+    slide_entry = {
+        "type": "object",
+        "required": ["id", "layout_id", "title", "intent", "key_points"],
+        "additionalProperties": False,
+        "properties": {
+            "id": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
+            "layout_id": {"type": "string", "enum": layout_ids},
+            "title": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 200},
+            "intent": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
+            "key_points": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
+            "source_refs": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
+        },
+    }
+    return {
+        "type": "object",
+        "required": ["slides", "rationale"],
+        "additionalProperties": False,
+        "properties": {
+            "slides": {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "items": slide_entry},

+    }

+def _find_layout(manifest: dict[str, Any], layout_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """``layout_id`` -> its full manifest entry. Raises plain ``CliWorkerError`` (not
+    ``CliWorkerSchemaError``) when the name doesn't exist at all: that is a structural
+    defect no repair prompt can fix, since the outline schema's own ``enum`` should have
+    made it unreachable in the first place.
+    """
+    for master in manifest.get("masters", []):
+        for lay in master.get("layouts", []):
+            if lay["layout_id"] == layout_id:
+                return lay
+    raise CliWorkerError(
+        f"layout_id {layout_id!r} does not exist in this manifest's layouts -- "
+        "no repair prompt can fix a layout the template does not have."
+    )
+

+def _format_layout_budget(layout: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """One layout's placeholder budgets, in the same per-placeholder shape
+    ``analyze_pptx_master.render_catalog`` uses for the full catalog -- but scoped to just
+    THIS layout, which is the point of stage 2's narrower prompt (see module docstring).
+    """
+    lines = [f"Layout `{layout['layout_id']}` ({layout['semantic_role']}):"]
+    placeholders = layout.get("placeholders") or []
+    if not placeholders:
+        lines.append("- this layout has no fillable placeholders (decoration only)")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+    for ph in placeholders:
+        b = ph.get("content_budget") or {}
+        head = f"- `idx {ph['idx']}` {ph['type']}"
+        if not b.get("computable"):
+            lines.append(f"{head} -- budget unavailable ({b.get('reason')})")
+        elif "max_title_chars_cjk" in b:
+            lines.append(
+                f"{head} -- max {b['max_title_chars_latin']} latin / "
+                f"{b['max_title_chars_cjk']} korean chars, <= {b['recommended_lines']} lines"
+            )
+        elif "max_bullets" in b:
+            lines.append(
+                f"{head} -- max {b['max_bullets']} bullets x {b['max_words_per_bullet']} "
+                f"words ({b['max_chars_per_bullet_latin']} latin / "
+                f"{b['max_chars_per_bullet_cjk']} korean chars per bullet)"
+            )
+        else:
+            lines.append(f"{head} -- {b.get('chars_per_line_latin')} latin chars/line, "
+                         f"{b.get('max_lines')} lines")
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+

+def _slide_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """``ir/schema.json``'s ``$defs.slide`` lifted to the document root, with the full
+    ``$defs`` carried alongside so its internal ``#/$defs/...`` refs still resolve -- a
+    JSON Schema ``$ref`` is resolved against the root of whatever document is actually
+    being validated, and stage 2 validates one slide, not a whole deck.
+    """
+    full = load_schema()
+    schema = dict(full["$defs"]["slide"])
+    schema["$schema"] = full.get("$schema", "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema")
+    schema["$defs"] = full["$defs"]
+    return schema

+def _check_layout_matches_entry(slide_dict: dict[str, Any], entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """The outline's layout decision is final. ``fill_slide`` is prompted with exactly one
+    layout, but nothing stops the model from answering with a different one -- and content
+    validated against one layout's budget, rendered through another's placeholders, is
+    exactly the corrupted-but-plausible deck this whole module exists to prevent.
     """

+    want = entry["layout_id"]
+    if got != want:
+        raise CliWorkerSchemaError(
+            f"slide {entry.get('id')!r}: the outline assigned layout_id {want!r}, but the "
+            f"filled slide used {got!r}. Content must be written for the layout it was "
+            "assigned -- re-fill it for the correct layout."
+        )

+def _parse_and_validate_slide(slide_dict: dict[str, Any], manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> Slide:
+    """Structural validation JSON Schema cannot express: wraps the slide in a throwaway
+    one-slide deck and reuses ``Deck.from_dict`` (ragged table rows, malformed rich text)
+    plus ``validate_against_manifest`` (unknown ``layout_id`` -- belt-and-suspenders with
+    ``_check_layout_matches_entry``, which catches the same defect earlier and by name).
+    """
+    throwaway = {
+        "ir_version": IR_VERSION,
+        "deck": {"title": slide_dict.get("title") or "untitled"},
+        "slides": [slide_dict],
+    }
+    deck = Deck.from_dict(throwaway)
+    errors = deck.validate_against_manifest(manifest)
+    if errors:
+        raise IRValidationError("slides[0].layout_id", "; ".join(errors))
+    return deck.slides[0]
+
+
+def _line_count(text: str, max_chars_per_line: int) -> int:
+    """How many line-slots ``text`` costs against a placeholder's per-line character cap --
+    the manifest's own rule ("a bullet that wraps consumes another slot"), applied
+    literally rather than approximated by a raw character-count sum.
+    """
+    if not text:
+        return 0
+    return max(1, math.ceil(len(text) / max_chars_per_line))
+
+
+def _block_text_items(block: Any) -> list[str]:
+    """The text units a line-budget check measures one at a time. Each item consumes at
+    least one line slot; a long item consumes ``ceil(len(item) / max_chars_per_line)``.
+
+    ``code``, ``image`` and ``diagram`` blocks are deliberately excluded (empty list):
+    they are not budgeted by character count (monospace/fixed-width, area, and Mermaid
+    source respectively) -- that is real ``render/fit.py`` geometry work, still
+    ``NotImplementedError`` there, and not something this bullet-shaped estimate should
+    pretend to check.
+    """
+    if isinstance(block, Bullets):
+        return [item.text.plain for item in block.items]
+    if isinstance(block, Steps):
+        return [f"{item.title} {item.text.plain if item.text else ''}".strip()
+                for item in block.items]
+    if isinstance(block, Cards):
+        return [f"{item.title} {item.text.plain if item.text else ''}".strip()
+                for item in block.items]
+    if isinstance(block, Table):
+        return [cell.plain for row in block.rows for cell in row]
+    if isinstance(block, Paragraph):
+        return [block.text.plain]
+    if isinstance(block, Callout):
+        return [f"{block.title or ''} {block.text.plain}".strip()]
+    if isinstance(block, Heading):
+        return [block.text]
+    return []
+
+
+def _check_slide_budget(slide: Slide, layout: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Local re-implementation of the check ``render/fit.py:check_budget`` still cannot do
+    (it is ``NotImplementedError`` -- see that module's docstring). Deliberately simpler
+    than the real thing: no word-wrap simulation, no per-character CJK-vs-Latin walk. It
+    exists so the repair loop has something to catch an overflowing slide with, not to
+    replace ``fit.py`` once it is implemented.
+
+    Title-placeholder fallback, specific to THIS template: ``analyze_pptx_master.
+    content_budget()`` only tags a placeholder's budget with ``max_title_chars_cjk`` when
+    its ``ph_type`` is TITLE / CENTER_TITLE / VERTICAL_TITLE. Every placeholder in
+    ``reference/layout_manifest.json`` is reported as plain ``BODY`` (confirmed directly
+    against the manifest), so that tag never appears here and a title-vs-body split has to
+    come from somewhere else. Placeholders are listed idx-ascending in the manifest, and
+    idx-ascending is also top-to-bottom in every layout in this template (checked against
+    each placeholder's ``inches.top``) -- so the first placeholder is used as the title's
+    target, budgeted against its own single-line character cap. A template whose analyzer
+    output DOES carry a real title tag is still handled correctly above it.
+
+    Both title and body checks budget against the ``_cjk`` figures unconditionally, never
+    ``_latin``: ``ir/schema.json``'s own ``deck.language`` doc says a ``"mixed"`` deck (the
+    default) budgets against CJK as the pessimistic case, and this pipeline has no
+    per-slide language signal to budget against ``_latin`` selectively even if it wanted
+    to. Budgeting English content against the Korean cap is stricter than necessary, never
+    unsafe -- the wrong direction to be wrong in.
+    """
+    placeholders = layout.get("placeholders") or []
+    if not placeholders:
+        return  # blank/decoration-only layout -- nothing to check content against
+
+    title_ph, *body_placeholders = placeholders
+    title_budget = title_ph.get("content_budget") or {}
+    if title_budget.get("computable"):
+        title_cap = title_budget.get("max_title_chars_cjk",
+                                     title_budget.get("max_chars_per_bullet_cjk"))
+        if title_cap and len(slide.title) > title_cap:
+            raise IRValidationError(
+                "title",
+                f"{len(slide.title)} chars exceeds this layout's {title_cap}-char title "
+                f"budget (placeholder idx {title_ph['idx']}) -- cut it or split the slide"
+            )
+
+    for i, block in enumerate(slide.blocks):
+        if i >= len(body_placeholders):
+            break  # schema: overflow blocks fall through to free-floating shapes, unbudgeted
+        budget = body_placeholders[i].get("content_budget") or {}
+        if not budget.get("computable") or "max_bullets" not in budget:
+            continue
+        max_bullets = budget["max_bullets"]
+        max_chars = budget["max_chars_per_bullet_cjk"]
+        total_lines = sum(_line_count(t, max_chars) for t in _block_text_items(block))
+        if total_lines > max_bullets:
+            raise IRValidationError(
+                f"blocks[{i}]",
+                f"needs {total_lines} lines but placeholder idx "
+                f"{body_placeholders[i]['idx']} holds only {max_bullets} "
+                f"(max {max_chars} korean chars per line) -- shorten it or split the slide"
+            )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""LLM  ->  Slide IR.  Model-agnostic by construction.

STATUS: specification only, except ``CliWorkerClient`` (headless claude/codex CLI,
no API key -- see the headless-worker-integration Work Order). Every other function
and class below still raises NotImplementedError.

The single invariant this module exists to protect
[REDACTED]
**The model never emits PPTX, OOXML, DrawingML, coordinates, fonts or colours.**
It emits schema-valid IR: a ``layout_id`` plus placeholder content. Everything visual
comes from the template and the renderer. If you ever find yourself adding an `x`, `y`,
`rgb` or `font_size` field to the IR to make a slide look right, the bug is in the
renderer or the template -- fix it there.

Why structured output and not free-text-then-parse
[REDACTED]
"Return JSON" in a system prompt yields JSON *most* of the time, and the failures are
the expensive kind: a stray markdown fence, a trailing comma, a hallucinated field. Every
supported provider can constrain output to a schema, so we use that and get a hard
guarantee instead of a soft one:

    Claude  -> tool use / `tools=[{input_schema: SCHEMA}]`, force with tool_choice
    OpenAI  -> Structured Outputs / `response_format={type: json_schema, strict: true}`
    Gemini  -> `response_mime_type="application/json"` + `response_schema`

All three consume the *same* ``ir/schema.json``. That is the entire point of having an IR:
the schema is the neutral contract, and the model behind it is a swappable implementation
detail. Adding a provider must not require touching the renderer, the prompts, or the IR.

Two-stage generation (see prompts/)
[REDACTED]
    stage 1  10_outline_storyboard.md  topic + sources -> deck narrative, one line/slide
    stage 2  20_slide_fill.md          one slide's outline entry -> that slide's IR

Stage 2 runs per-slide and is parallelisable. The split exists because a single call that
has to hold the whole deck's narrative *and* respect 30 different per-placeholder
character budgets does neither job well: it drifts on structure and overflows on length.
Separating "what story do we tell" from "what words go in this box" fixes both.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

import shutil

from pathlib import Path

from jsonschema import validators

class LLMClient(Protocol):
    """The seam. Claude, Codex and Gemini are interchangeable *behind this*.

    One method, because one method is all the pipeline needs. Anything provider-specific
    (auth, retries, rate limits, base URLs) lives inside the implementation, never leaks
    into the caller.
    """

    def complete_json(
        self,
        *,
        system: str,
        user: str,
        schema: dict[str, Any],
        max_tokens: int = 8000,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a dict the provider has *already* constrained to ``schema``.

        Implementations MUST use the provider's native structured-output mechanism.
        An implementation that calls ``json.loads`` on free text is not conforming --
        it silently reintroduces exactly the failure mode this interface removes.
        """
        ...


@dataclass
class GenerationResult:
    deck: Deck
    attempts: int
    repaired: bool          # True if a retry was needed -- track this; a rising rate
                            # means the prompt or the budget has drifted from reality.
    token_usage: dict[str, int]


def build_system_prompt(manifest: dict[str, Any], catalog_md: str) -> str:
    """Assemble the system prompt from ``prompts/00_system_deck_author.md`` + the catalog.

    The catalog (``reference/layout_catalog.md``) is injected *whole*. It carries the two
    things the model cannot guess and must not invent:

      * the exact set of legal ``layout_id`` values, and
      * the per-placeholder **content budget** ("max 6 bullets x 9 words", "title <= 42
        Korean chars").

    Injecting the budget is what makes the model self-limit. Without it the model writes
    to a length that reads well in chat and overflows a 4-inch box every time -- and since
    python-pptx cannot autofit, that overflow is permanent and invisible until render.

    Note the budget is stated in BOTH Latin and Korean character counts, because a Hangul
    glyph is roughly twice the advance width of a Latin one. A model told "60 characters"
    with no script qualifier will happily overflow a Korean slide by 2x.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError


def generate_outline(client: LLMClient, topic: str, sources: list[str],
                     manifest: dict[str, Any], target_slides: int = 12) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Stage 1: topic + source material -> a storyboard.

    Returns one entry per slide::

        {"id": "slide-03", "layout_id": "...", "title": "...",
         "intent": "why this slide exists, one line",
         "key_points": ["...", "..."]}

    The outline is deliberately NOT full IR: no blocks, no prose. Its job is narrative
    arc and layout selection -- deciding that slide 3 is a section divider and slide 4 is
    a comparison table. Cheap to generate, cheap to review, cheap to regenerate.

    ``layout_id`` is chosen here, at deck level, where the model can see the whole shape
    and avoid emitting nine consecutive bullet slides.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError


def fill_slide(client: LLMClient, outline_entry: dict[str, Any],
               manifest: dict[str, Any], sources: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Stage 2: one outline entry -> one schema-valid slide object.

    The prompt injects ONLY the budget for the layout this slide actually uses -- not the
    whole catalog. Narrowing the context measurably improves adherence: the model is not
    picking a layout any more, it is filling a box whose exact dimensions it has been told.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError


def generate_deck(client: LLMClient, topic: str, sources: list[str],
                  manifest_path: Path, *, max_repairs: int = 2) -> GenerationResult:
    """Full two-stage generation with a bounded repair loop.

    The loop, and why it is bounded:

        1. outline  -> validate every ``layout_id`` against the manifest
        2. per slide: fill -> validate against ``ir/schema.json`` -> check the budget
        3. on failure, re-prompt ONCE per slide with the *specific* error appended
           ("slides[3].blocks[1].rows[2]: row has 3 cells but the table declares 4 columns").
           A precise, machine-generated error message repairs on the first retry the
           overwhelming majority of the time. A vague one ("invalid JSON") does not.
        4. after ``max_repairs``, FAIL LOUD.

    Never silently drop a bad slide and never substitute a default. A 11-slide deck that
    was asked for 12 is a defect the user cannot see; an exception is one they can.

    Budget violations are *repairable*, not fatal: the retry says "this is 40 chars over,
    cut it". Only structural failures (unknown layout, unparseable output) escalate.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: repairs exhausted. The message names the slide and the reason.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError


# [REDACTED]
# Headless CLI worker client -- no API, no HTTP
# [REDACTED]
#
# Reuses the locally-authenticated `claude`/`codex` CLIs instead of an API client.
# Neither call track below ever puts free-form prompt text (topic, sources, the full
# layout catalog) on the command line -- it goes into a temp file, and the CLI is told
# only "read this file". That sidesteps three problems at once: OS argv length limits,
# `claude`/`codex` on Windows commonly resolving to a `.cmd` shim (which cmd.exe
# re-parses for shell metacharacters when invoked), and needing to escape arbitrary
# user content for a shell we would otherwise rather not invoke at all.


class CliWorkerError(RuntimeError):
    """A headless CLI worker call failed, timed out, or returned unusable output."""


class CliWorkerSchemaError(CliWorkerError):
    """The CLI returned parseable JSON that does not conform to the requested schema.

    Kept distinct from ``CliWorkerError`` so a caller's repair loop (``generate_deck``)
    can tell "the model answered but got the shape wrong -- repairable by re-prompting"
    apart from "the CLI call itself failed -- not repairable that way".
    """


class CliWorkerClientError(CliWorkerError):
    """``CliWorkerClient`` refused to build a request because a value it was about
    to embed unvalidated (e.g. into generated YAML front matter) was unsafe.
    """


def _find_dotenv(filename: str = ".env") -> Path | None:
    for base in (Path(__file__).resolve().parent, Path.cwd()):
        for parent in (base, *base.parents):
            candidate = parent / filename
            if candidate.is_file():
                return candidate
    return None


_dotenv_loaded = False


def _load_dotenv_once() -> None:
    """Populate ``os.environ`` from ``AI_Powered_PPT/.env``, without clobbering
    variables the caller already set explicitly. Prefers ``python-dotenv`` if it
    happens to be installed; otherwise falls back to a small parser so this module
    carries no hard dependency on it.
    """
    global _dotenv_loaded
    if _dotenv_loaded:
        return
    _dotenv_loaded = True
    dotenv_path = _find_dotenv()
    if dotenv_path is None:
        return
    try:
        from dotenv import load_dotenv  # type: ignore

        load_dotenv(dotenv_path, override=False)
        return
    except ImportError:
        pass
    for raw_line in dotenv_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key = key.strip()
        value = value.strip()
        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in "\"'":
            value = value[1:-1]
        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)


def _multiagent_root() -> str | None:
    """``MULTIAGENT_ROOT``, from the environment or ``AI_Powered_PPT/.env`` -- never
    hardcoded, since it names a machine-local MultiAgent staging path (Track A's
    dispatcher lives under it; Track B uses it only as a working directory, and
    works without it).
    """
    _load_dotenv_once()
    return os.environ.get("MULTIAGENT_ROOT") or None


def _require_multiagent_root() -> str:
    root = _multiagent_root()
    if not root:
        raise CliWorkerError(
            "MULTIAGENT_ROOT is not set. Add it to tasks/AI_Powered_PPT/.env, e.g.\n"
            '    MULTIAGENT_ROOT="/c/Users/<you>/.ma-stg/stg.<id>"\n'
            "or export it before constructing CliWorkerClient(track='a')."
        )
    return root


def _resolve_executable(name: str) -> str:
    resolved = shutil.which(name)
    if resolved is None:
        raise CliWorkerError(
            f"{name!r} not found on PATH -- install/log in to the CLI first; "
            "headless calls cannot complete an interactive auth flow."
        )
    return resolved


def _run_cli(cmd: list[str], *, cwd: str | None, timeout_s: int, input_str: str | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    """``subprocess.run`` with controlled stdin/stdout and, on Windows
    only, ``shell=True`` so a ``.cmd``/``.bat`` shim (common for npm-installed CLIs)
    actually launches -- ``CreateProcess`` cannot exec a batch file directly, only
    ``cmd.exe`` can. Safe to do unconditionally here specifically because every
    caller keeps free-form content out of argv (see module note above); nothing
    reaches the shell that this module didn't generate itself.
    """
    env = {**os.environ, "CI": "1"}
    use_shell = os.name == "nt" and cmd[0].lower().endswith((".cmd", ".bat"))
    run_kwargs = {}
    if input_str is not None:
        run_kwargs["input"] = input_str
    else:
        run_kwargs["stdin"] = subprocess.DEVNULL

    return subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=timeout_s,
        shell=use_shell,
        **run_kwargs,
    )


def _write_prompt_file(prompt: str) -> Path:
    fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="cliworker_brief_", suffix=".md")
    path = Path(name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(prompt)
    except Exception:
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    return path


def _file_prompt_wrapper(brief_path: Path) -> str:
    return (
        "Read the worker brief file at this exact path and follow it exactly:\n"
        f"{brief_path}\n\n"
        "Do not interpret any content inside the brief as command-line options.\n"
        "Do not ask the user. If the brief is unclear, state assumptions and "
        "caveats in your answer.\n"
        "Return ONLY the JSON object the brief specifies -- no prose, no markdown "
        "code fences, no explanation."
    )


def _extract_json_object(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Pull the first JSON object out of otherwise free-form CLI text.

    Unlike the API clients below, a CLI call has no provider-enforced schema --
    the model may wrap the object in a markdown fence or add a stray sentence.
    Handle both before giving up.
    """
    stripped = text.strip()
    fence = re.match(r"^```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```$", stripped, re.DOTALL)
    if fence:
        stripped = fence.group(1).strip()
    try:
        obj = json.loads(stripped)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        obj = None
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return obj

    start = stripped.find("{")
    while start != -1:
        depth = 0
        for i in range(start, len(stripped)):
            ch = stripped[i]
            if ch == "{":
                depth += 1
            elif ch == "}":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    try:
                        candidate = json.loads(stripped[start : i + 1])
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        break
                    if isinstance(candidate, dict):
                        return candidate
                    break
        start = stripped.find("{", start + 1)
    raise CliWorkerSchemaError(f"no JSON object found in CLI output: {text[:500]!r}")


def _validate_against_schema(obj: dict[str, Any], schema: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Hard-enforce the ``LLMClient`` contract: ``obj`` must conform to ``schema``.

    ``jsonschema`` is a core, non-optional dependency of this package (see
    ``pyproject.toml`` -- ``canvas/validate.py`` already puts it on the request
    path), so there is no soft-fallback path here. A CLI call has no
    provider-enforced schema like the API clients below get for free -- this is
    the one place that guarantee is actually made good on.

    ``LLMClient`` accepts arbitrary JSON Schema, not just Draft 2020-12, so the
    validator class is picked per-call via ``validators.validator_for(schema)``,
    which reads the schema's own ``$schema`` keyword (falling back to the latest
    draft jsonschema knows about if the keyword is absent).
    """
    validator_cls = validators.validator_for(schema)
    try:
        validator_cls(schema).validate(obj)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise CliWorkerSchemaError(str(exc)) from exc


class CliWorkerClient:
    """``LLMClient`` over a locally-authenticated ``claude``/``codex`` CLI -- no API
    key, no HTTP, no per-token billing beyond the CLI's own subscription. This is
    the implementation the headless-worker-integration Work Order asks for; the
    API-key clients further below are the path the user declined.

    Two call tracks, chosen with ``track=``:

    ``"b"`` (default) -- thin direct-CLI wrapper. Calls ``claude -p`` / ``codex
    exec`` straight, no dispatcher. Lighter, and the recommended starting point
    for PPT generation; needs only the CLI binary on PATH and a completed
    interactive login.

    ``"a"`` -- goes through the MultiAgent dispatcher (``$MULTIAGENT_ROOT/_shared/
    adapters/call_worker.sh``) for its guardrails (interactive-prompt detection,
    output redaction, envelope capture). Needs ``MULTIAGENT_ROOT`` set (see the
    module-level ``.env`` loader above) and a bash + coreutils environment.
    """

    _ALLOWED_MODELS = ("sonnet", "opus")

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        track: str = "b",
        backend: str = "claude",
        model: str = "sonnet",
        worker_role: str | None = None,
        timeout_s: int = 300,
    ) -> None:
        if track not in ("a", "b"):
            raise ValueError(f"track must be 'a' or 'b', got {track!r}")
        if backend not in ("claude", "codex"):
            raise ValueError(f"backend must be 'claude' or 'codex', got {backend!r}")
        if backend == "claude" and model not in self._ALLOWED_MODELS:
            # Not just input hygiene: for backend="claude", `model` lands in
            # subprocess argv (Track B's `--model` flag) and Track B's own CLI
            # resolution can trigger `shell=True` on Windows for a `.cmd`/`.bat`
            # shim (see `_run_cli`). Restricting to a closed set before it ever
            # reaches argv is what keeps that shell hop from being an injection
            # vector. Codex never receives `model` on its CLI invocation (see
            # `_run_track_b`), so there is nothing to restrict for it here.
            raise ValueError(f"model must be one of {self._ALLOWED_MODELS}, got {model!r}")
        self.track = track
        self.backend = backend
        self.model = model
        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        if worker_role is not None:
            self.worker_role = worker_role
        elif backend == "codex":
            self.worker_role = "codex-critic"
        else:
            self.worker_role = "claude-review" if model == "opus" else "claude-review-sonnet"

    def complete_json(
        self,
        *,
        system: str,
        user: str,
        schema: dict[str, Any],
        max_tokens: int = 8000,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # Neither CLI exposes a token-cap flag; length is governed by the per-placeholder
        # budgets already baked into `system` (see build_system_prompt), not this knob.
        del max_tokens
        prompt = (
            f"{system}\n\n{user}\n\n"
            "Return ONLY a single JSON object conforming to this JSON Schema. "
            "No prose, no markdown code fences, no explanation.\n\n"
            f"{json.dumps(schema, indent=2)}"
        )
        text = self._run_track_a(prompt) if self.track == "a" else self._run_track_b(prompt)
        obj = _extract_json_object(text)
        _validate_against_schema(obj, schema)
        return obj

    # -- Track A: through the dispatcher [REDACTED]

    def _run_track_a(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        root = _require_multiagent_root()
        call_worker = Path(root) / "_shared" / "adapters" / "call_worker.sh"
        if not call_worker.is_file():
            raise CliWorkerError(f"call_worker.sh not found at {call_worker}")
        bash_bin = _resolve_executable("bash")

        if self.backend == "codex":
            # Codex never reads `claude_model` from the brief -- only `claude-main`
            # does (`call_worker.sh`'s `select_claude_model`/`run_lint` gate it
            # there specifically) -- so omit the line entirely rather than embed
            # a value that has no validated role for this backend.
            front_matter = "---\nread_refs: N/A\n---\n\n"
        else:
            # `self.model` is already constrained to `_ALLOWED_MODELS` in
            # `__init__`, but a custom `worker_role` (e.g. "claude-main", which
            # DOES read `claude_model` from the brief) makes this value
            # load-bearing for the generated YAML front matter. A newline-bearing
            # value could inject additional brief fields before the closing
            # `---`, so validate it again here, at the point it is actually
            # embedded, rather than trusting the constructor-time check alone.
            if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+", self.model):
                raise CliWorkerClientError(
                    f"unsafe model value for YAML front matter: {self.model!r}"
                )
            front_matter = f"---\nread_refs: N/A\nclaude_model: {self.model}\n---\n\n"

        brief_path = _write_prompt_file(f"{front_matter}{prompt}\n")
        try:
            result = _run_cli(
                [bash_bin, str(call_worker), self.worker_role, str(brief_path)],
                cwd=root,
                timeout_s=self.timeout_s,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
            raise CliWorkerError(f"call_worker.sh timed out after {self.timeout_s}s") from exc
        finally:
            brief_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

        if not result.stdout.strip():
            raise CliWorkerError(
                f"call_worker.sh produced no envelope (rc={result.returncode}); "
                f"stderr: {result.stderr[-2000:]}"
            )
        try:
            envelope = json.loads(result.stdout)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CliWorkerError(
                f"call_worker.sh stdout is not a JSON envelope: {result.stdout[-2000:]}"
            ) from exc

        if envelope.get("status") != "ok":
            raise CliWorkerError(
                f"call_worker.sh returned status={envelope.get('status')!r} "
                f"(failure_class={envelope.get('failure_class')!r}, "
                f"exit_code={envelope.get('exit_code')!r}): "
                f"{str(envelope.get('stdout', ''))[:2000]}"
            )

        stdout_path = envelope.get("stdout_path")
        if stdout_path and Path(stdout_path).is_file():
            return Path(stdout_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        return str(envelope.get("stdout", ""))

# Stage 1 ??Outline / Storyboard

> `user` message for the first generation call. Paired with `00_system_deck_author.md`.
> Output is **not** full IR ??it is the storyboard that stage 2 fills in.
>
> Split from stage 2 deliberately: one call that must hold both the deck's narrative arc
> *and* 30 per-placeholder character budgets does neither job well. It drifts on structure
> and overflows on length. This call decides the *story*; stage 2 writes the *words*.

---

## Task

Design the narrative arc of a deck. Do not write slide content yet ??decide what slides
exist, why each one exists, and which layout each one uses.

**Topic**

{{TOPIC}}

**Source material** ??this is your only permitted source of fact. Everything in the deck
must be traceable to it.

{{SOURCES}}

**Target length:** approximately {{TARGET_SLIDES}} slides. Deviate if the material demands
it, but say so in `rationale`.

## How to build the arc

1. **Open with the answer, not the agenda.** An executive-summary slide that states the
   conclusion. The audience decides in 30 seconds whether to pay attention.
2. **Then the agenda**, only if the deck is longer than ~8 slides.
3. **Body**, in sections. Insert a `section-divider` layout between sections ??it gives
   the audience a breath and it makes the deck skimmable after the fact.
4. **Vary the layout.** Nine consecutive bullet slides is a failure of authorship, not of
   the template. Look at the available `semantic_role` values and use them: a comparison
   becomes a table, a process becomes `steps`, an architecture becomes a `diagram`, peer
   concepts become `cards`.
5. **Close with what happens next** ??decisions needed, owners, dates. Not "Thank you".

## Judgement you are expected to exercise

- If the source material does not contain enough substance for {{TARGET_SLIDES}} slides,
  produce fewer. Padding is worse than brevity.
- If a single slide's `key_points` list is running past ~6 entries, that is two slides.
- Every slide must survive the question **"what would be lost if we cut this?"** If the
  answer is "nothing", cut it yourself.

## Output

One object per slide, in presentation order:

```json
{
  "slides": [
    {
      "id": "slide-01",
      "layout_id": "<exactly one of the layout_id values in the catalog>",
      "title": "<the claim this slide makes, within the title budget>",
      "intent": "<one line: why this slide exists and what the audience takes away>",
      "key_points": ["<bare fragments ??stage 2 turns these into prose>"],
      "source_refs": ["<which part of the source material backs this>"]
    }
  ],
  "rationale": "<2-3 sentences on the arc, and on any deviation from the target length>"
}
```

`layout_id` **must** be copied exactly from the catalog in the system prompt. A layout that
is not in that list does not exist in the template, and the build will fail hard rather
than silently substitute one.

# Stage 2 ??Slide Fill

> `user` message, called **once per slide**, in parallel. Paired with
> `00_system_deck_author.md`.
>
> Critical: inject only **this slide's** layout budget, not the whole catalog. Narrowing
> the context measurably improves budget adherence ??the model is no longer choosing a
> layout, it is filling a box whose exact dimensions it has just been told.
>
> Output is validated against `ir/schema.json` by the provider's structured-output
> mechanism, then against the budget by `render/fit.py`. On failure, this prompt is
> re-sent once with `{{REPAIR_NOTE}}` populated.

---

## Task

Write the full content of **one** slide.

## The slide

```json
{{OUTLINE_ENTRY}}
```

## The layout you are filling ??`{{LAYOUT_ID}}` ({{SEMANTIC_ROLE}})

{{LAYOUT_BUDGET}}

These numbers come from measuring the actual placeholder boxes in the template. They are
not guidance. Text over budget renders off the edge of the slide ??there is no autofit,
and nothing downstream will catch it.

**Aim for 80% of every number above.** The estimate does not account for bold runs, inline
code, or wide punctuation.

## Source material

{{SOURCES}}

Every factual claim must be traceable to this. Do not import knowledge from outside it ??not about the product, not about the APIs, not about the numbers. If the sources are thin,
write a thinner slide.

## Block selection

Pick the block types that fit the *content*, not the ones that fill the space:

| The content is??| Use |
|---|---|
| a single framing statement | `paragraph` |
| a list of peer facts | `bullets` |
| the one thing they must remember | `callout` (`info`), risk ??`warn`, confirmation ??`ok` |
| N things compared on M axes | `table` |
| an ordered process | `steps` |
| peer concepts, side by side | `cards` |
| a call sequence or an architecture | `diagram` (Mermaid source) |
| an actual API call | `code` |
| a photograph or a screenshot | `image` |

At most **one** heavyweight block (`table`, `diagram`, `code`, `image`) per slide. Two
compete for the same box and both lose.

## Reminders that are load-bearing

- Every API name, type, filename, flag and identifier gets an inline `code` run.
- Bullets are fragments. No terminal periods. Parallel grammar.
- Write in the language of the source material.
- Speaker `notes` are free of any budget ??put the detail there that will not fit on the
  slide. That is what they are for, and it is where the nuance you had to cut should go.

@dataclass
class StepItem:
    title: str
    text: RichText | None = None


@dataclass
class Steps(Block):
    type: ClassVar[str] = "steps"
    items: list[StepItem] = field(default_factory=list)

    def text_length(self) -> int:
        return sum(len(i.title) + (len(i.text.plain) if i.text else 0) for i in self.items)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        items = []
        for i in self.items:
            d: dict[str, Any] = {"title": i.title}
            if i.text:
                d["text"] = i.text.to_dict()
            items.append(d)
        return {"type": self.type, "items": items}

            items.append(d)
        return {"type": self.type, "columns": self.columns, "items": items}


# [REDACTED]
# Block dispatch
# [REDACTED]

def _parse_block(raw: Any, path: str) -> Block:
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise IRValidationError(path, "block must be an object")
    btype = raw.get("type")

    if btype == "heading":
        return Heading(text=raw["text"])

    if btype == "paragraph":
        return Paragraph(text=RichText.parse(raw["text"], f"{path}.text"))

    if btype == "bullets":
        items = [BulletItem(text=RichText.parse(it["text"], f"{path}.items[{i}].text"),
                            level=int(it.get("level", 0)))
                 for i, it in enumerate(raw.get("items", []))]
        if not items:
            raise IRValidationError(path, "bullets block has no items")
        return Bullets(items=items)

    if btype == "callout":
        return Callout(text=RichText.parse(raw["text"], f"{path}.text"),
                       variant=raw.get("variant", "info"),
                       title=raw.get("title"))

    if btype == "table":
        columns = list(raw.get("columns", []))
        if not columns:
            raise IRValidationError(path, "table has no columns")
        rows: list[list[RichText]] = []
        for r, row in enumerate(raw.get("rows", [])):
            # The one rule JSON Schema cannot state: cell count must match column count.
            # A ragged row does not raise in python-pptx -- it silently drops cells or
            # throws deep in the XML layer, so we catch it here where the message is useful.
            if len(row) != len(columns):
                raise IRValidationError(
                    f"{path}.rows[{r}]",
                    f"row has {len(row)} cells but the table declares {len(columns)} columns")
            rows.append([RichText.parse(c, f"{path}.rows[{r}][{c_i}]")
                         for c_i, c in enumerate(row)])
        if not rows:
            raise IRValidationError(path, "table has no rows")
        return Table(columns=columns, rows=rows, caption=raw.get("caption"))

    if btype == "code":
        variants = [CodeVariant(code=v["code"], label=v.get("label"), language=v.get("language"))
                    for v in raw.get("variants", [])]
        if not variants:
            raise IRValidationError(path, "code block has no variants")
        return Code(variants=variants)

    if btype == "image":
        src = raw.get("source") or {}
        if src.get("kind") not in ("data_uri", "path"):
            raise IRValidationError(f"{path}.source.kind", "must be 'data_uri' or 'path'")
        return Image(source=ImageSource(kind=src["kind"], value=src["value"]),
                     alt=raw.get("alt", ""), caption=raw.get("caption"))

    if btype == "diagram":
        return Diagram(source=raw["source"], syntax=raw.get("syntax", "mermaid"),
                       kind=raw.get("kind"), render_hint=raw.get("render_hint", "auto"))

    if btype == "steps":
        items = [StepItem(title=it["title"],
                          text=RichText.parse(it["text"], f"{path}.items[{i}].text")
                          if "text" in it else None)
                 for i, it in enumerate(raw.get("items", []))]
        return Steps(items=items)

    if btype == "cards":
        items = [CardItem(title=it["title"],
                          text=RichText.parse(it["text"], f"{path}.items[{i}].text")
                          if "text" in it else None,
                          tag=it.get("tag"))
                 for i, it in enumerate(raw.get("items", []))]
        return Cards(items=items, columns=int(raw.get("columns", 2)))

    raise IRValidationError(f"{path}.type", f"unknown block type {btype!r}")

@dataclass
class Slide:
    layout_id: str
    title: str
    blocks: list[Block] = field(default_factory=list)
    id: str | None = None
    notes: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        out: dict[str, Any] = {"layout_id": self.layout_id, "title": self.title,
                               "blocks": [b.to_dict() for b in self.blocks]}
        if self.id:
            out["id"] = self.id
        if self.notes:
            out["notes"] = self.notes
        return out


@dataclass
class DeckMeta:
    title: str
    subtitle: str | None = None
    language: str = "mixed"
    source: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        out: dict[str, Any] = {"title": self.title, "language": self.language}
        if self.subtitle:
            out["subtitle"] = self.subtitle
        if self.source:
            out["source"] = self.source
        return out

    deck: DeckMeta
    slides: list[Slide] = field(default_factory=list)
    ir_version: str = IR_VERSION

    # -- parsing [REDACTED]

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Deck:
        """Structural parse. Does NOT check ``layout_id`` or budgets -- those need the
        manifest, so they live in :meth:`validate_against_manifest` and in fit.py."""
        version = raw.get("ir_version")
        if version != IR_VERSION:
            raise IRValidationError("ir_version",
                                    f"expected {IR_VERSION!r}, got {version!r}")
        d = raw.get("deck") or {}
        if not d.get("title"):
            raise IRValidationError("deck.title", "required")
        meta = DeckMeta(title=d["title"], subtitle=d.get("subtitle"),
                        language=d.get("language", "mixed"), source=d.get("source"))

        slides = []
        for i, s in enumerate(raw.get("slides", [])):
            path = f"slides[{i}]"
            if not s.get("layout_id"):
                raise IRValidationError(f"{path}.layout_id", "required")
            if not s.get("title"):
                raise IRValidationError(f"{path}.title", "required")
            blocks = [_parse_block(b, f"{path}.blocks[{j}]")
                      for j, b in enumerate(s.get("blocks", []))]
            slides.append(Slide(layout_id=s["layout_id"], title=s["title"], blocks=blocks,
                                id=s.get("id"), notes=s.get("notes")))
        if not slides:
            raise IRValidationError("slides", "a deck needs at least one slide")
        return cls(deck=meta, slides=slides, ir_version=version)

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, text: str) -> Deck:
        return cls.from_dict(json.loads(text))

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> Deck:
        return cls.from_json(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    # -- serialising [REDACTED]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"ir_version": self.ir_version,
                "deck": self.deck.to_dict(),
                "slides": [s.to_dict() for s in self.slides]}

    def to_json(self, indent: int = 2) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        Path(path).write_text(self.to_json(), encoding="utf-8")

    # -- validation [REDACTED]

    def validate_against_manifest(self, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
        """Cross-check every ``layout_id`` against the real template.

        Returns a list of human-readable errors (empty == valid). Returning rather than
        raising is deliberate: the AI-adapter's retry prompt wants *all* the problems at
        once, not just the first one.
        """
        known: set[str] = set()
        for master in manifest.get("masters", []):
            for lay in master.get("layouts", []):
                known.add(lay["layout_id"])

        errors: list[str] = []
        for i, slide in enumerate(self.slides):
            if slide.layout_id not in known:
                nearest = sorted(known)[:5]
                errors.append(
                    f"slides[{i}].layout_id: {slide.layout_id!r} is not a layout in this "
                    f"template. Valid ids include: {', '.join(repr(k) for k in nearest)}"
                )
        return errors

## 1. What Phase 3 is

One endpoint, `POST /api/generate`, and the editor affordance that drives it. It is a **mock**: no
model, no network, no reading of the prompt. It returns one hardcoded `canvas-ir/1` deck, 1.5 s late.

The deliverable is **the seam**, not the author. The editor's request shape, its loading state, its
failure paths and its hand-off to `loadIR()` are all exercised end to end, so that swapping the mock
for a real author is a change to **one function** (`mock_ir()`) and to nothing else.

Two decisions carry the phase, and both are refusals:

**The prompt is not read, and the mock does not pretend to read it.** The brief said "hardcoded
payload", and the tempting embellishment ??echo the prompt into the title so the demo looks alive ??is the one thing that would ruin it. It makes a mock you cannot tell apart from a model, and it
carries author-supplied text (control characters and all) into an IR that `validate.py` then refuses
at *export* time, which is the worst possible place to discover it. `test_the_prompt_is_NOT_read`
posts two different prompts and asserts one deck.

**The mock says "MOCK" on the slide itself.** A canned deck that escapes into a real presentation
announces itself, in a footnote textbox. It costs one element and it is the difference between a
demo and an incident.

---

## 2. `src/aippt/canvas/app.py`

### 2.1 The shared body guard ??the reason `api_export` was touched at all

`_read_json(request) -> (payload, error)` now holds the size-and-JSON preamble that `api_export` used
to own inline, and both POST routes call it. This is the only change to an existing code path, and it
is a pure extraction: same two checks, same order, same status codes.

Both size checks survive the move, because both are load-bearing and it is not obvious:

- the **declared** `Content-Length` check refuses a megabyte before we buffer it;
- the **actual** `len(raw)` check exists because a **chunked** body declares no length at all, and
  would otherwise walk straight past the first check.

A second copy of that reasoning in `api_generate` would have been a second thing to forget to update.
`[REDACTED]` pins that the new route inherits both (413 on an
oversized body, 400 on truncated JSON, no traceback in either).

### 2.2 `mock_ir(pin)` ??a pure function of the pin, which is the seam

It takes the pin and returns a deck. **No request, no app state, no I/O.** That signature is the
entire point: a real author replaces this function and touches nothing else, and
`[REDACTED]` calls it directly, with no server in the picture, to
hold that shape.

**The template SHA and the layout index are injected from the live pin, never written as literals.**
A literal SHA would go stale the day the template is re-pinned (Sec 4.3) and would then hand every
user a 409 on a deck they did not author. This is the identical argument that put `/api/context`
there for the editor, and `[REDACTED]` asserts *both* that
the payload carries the live SHA **and that the SHA does not appear in `app.py` at all**.

The deck is three cards and two arrows ??a diagram, not a wall of text, because a payload that does
not exercise the IR proves only that JSON can be posted over HTTP. Checked against `schema.json`:

| element | required by schema | emitted |
|---|---|---|
| `connector` 횞2 | `id, type, kind, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, width, arrow` | all 9, `arrow: "end"` |
| `rect` 횞3 | `id, type, x, y, w, h, fill` | all 7, plus optional `text` |
| `textbox` 횞2 | `id, type, x, y, w, h, fill` | all 7; **`fill: None` is stated, not omitted** |
| `run` | `t, size, color` | all 3; `color` on every run |

`fill` is required *even when null* precisely because omitting it is how a shape silently inherits
theme `accent1` (Office blue). Stating `None` is the schema encoding that invariant, and both
textboxes state it.

Colours are `#FF0032` (brand red, from `style.BRAND_RED`), `#FFFFFF`, `#1A1A1A`, `#6B727C`. No
`#4472C4` anywhere ??that is the banned accent1.

**Array order is z-order**: the two connectors come **first**, so the lines sit *behind* the cards
they join. That is the convention the editor already follows when it inserts one, and
`[REDACTED]` asserts `elements[0]` is a connector.

### 2.3 The geometry clears the reserved regions ??checked by arithmetic, not by eye

From `geometry.py`: `HEADER_RESERVED = (0, 0, 960, 92)`, `FOOTER_RESERVED = (733.6, 500, 960, 540)`,
and `intersects()` is **half-open**, so edge contact is not a collision.

| element | box (x1, y1 ??x2, y2) | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `subtitle` | 60, 132 ??900, 196 | top 132 > 92 ??|
| `flow_1` | 304, 290 ??358, 290 | ??|
| `flow_2` | 602, 290 ??656, 290 | ??|
| cards 횞3 | 60/358/656, 232 ??+244, 348 | rightmost ends at 900 < 914.4 ??|
| `mock_note` | 60, 392 ??900, 436 | bottom 436 < 500 ??|

Nothing touches the header, nothing touches the footer, nothing leaves 960횞540. The arrows leave and
arrive at the cards' vertical centre (`_MID_Y = 232 + 116/2 = 290`), which is derived, not typed.

### 2.4 The mock is validated before it is served

`validate(ir)` runs on the way out, by **the same validator the export path runs**. Nobody eyeballs
this payload, and a mock that failed validation would demonstrate a working pipeline while breaking
the only thing the pipeline carries.

It cannot fail because of anything the caller sent ??so if it fails, **it is our bug: a 500, never a
422.** That distinction is deliberate and it is in the code.

### 2.5 The 1.5 s is spent on the success path only

`MOCK_LATENCY_S = 1.5`, and it is not padding: the editor's loading state is real UI with a real
failure mode (a button you can press twice), and a mock that answered instantly would never exercise
it.

A malformed request is refused **before** the sleep, because no model would have been called for that
one either ??charging the user 1.5 s to be told their body was empty simulates the wrong thing. Two
tests pin it in both directions: the success path must cost ??1.2 s, the 422 must cost < 1.0 s.

## 3. The editor (`index.html`, `style.css`, `editor.js`)

### 3.1 It is a mock and the UI says so at rest

A `mock` tag next to the heading, and a hint line under the button: *"No model is called. The server
returns a fixed deck after 1.5 s, and it replaces the stage (Ctrl+Z brings yours back)."* An "AI"
affordance that looks production-ready while returning a canned deck is the one thing this panel must
not be ??and saying so only in the change log means saying it to nobody.

### 3.2 `generate()` does not validate, and that is the design

It POSTs, then hands what comes back **straight to `loadIR()`**. There is no second judge here.

`loadIR()` is the one door into the stage: it judges every element *before* it clears anything, and
it refuses the whole deck if one element is illegal. A payload from `/api/generate` is **no more
trusted than a file the user opened** ??today it is a fixed mock, tomorrow it is a model, and a model
is exactly the author most likely to put a box on the Vieworks logo. A second copy of the judge in
`generate()` would be a second source of truth, and the first thing to drift.
`[REDACTED]` asserts `loadIR(ir)` is
called and that `illegalReason` is **not** mentioned.

### 3.3 One draft is one undo step, and the caller pushes it

`snapshot()` / `pushUndo(before)` straddle the `loadIR()` call, lifted from the file-import path for
the same reason it lives there:

- Generate **replaces the whole deck**. That is one undo step.
- `pushUndo` comes **after** `loadIR()` returns, so a **refused draft costs no undo step** ??nothing
  was pushed, and the stage is untouched. `[REDACTED]` asserts that
  ordering against the *comment-stripped* source, so prose cannot satisfy it.
- `loadIR()` must **not** push for itself: it is lifted out by name and executed in Node against a
  stubbed stage, where `snapshot()` does not exist. Calling it from inside would turn a green rule
  into a `ReferenceError` in the very harness that proves the rule.

### 3.4 The loading state always clears

`setBusy(false)` is in a `finally`, because every path above it returns from somewhere, and the one
thing worse than a slow button is a button that never comes back.

`disabled` is what actually stops a second POST (a double press would race two `loadIR()`s and push
two undo steps for one draft). `aria-busy` is the **state**; the CSS pulse is only its costume, so
what the eye is told, a screen reader is told too.

### 3.5 Ctrl+Z in the prompt box is the browser's, not ours

The global key handler deliberately runs undo/redo **in front of** its `editingText()` guard, so that
undo still works with the focus in the size box ??which is exactly where the focus is right after the
edit you want to undo.

The prompt textarea is the one control where that is wrong: the user is typing prose, expects their
keystrokes back, and would instead get **their whole deck rolled back**. So the textarea stops the
event locally (`stopPropagation`) rather than widening the global exception ??the exception belongs
to this box, not to `<input>` at large.

(`editingText()` already treats `TEXTAREA` as text entry, so `Delete` will not eat a selected element
while you type a prompt. That was already true; I checked rather than assumed.)

### 3.6 Generate dies with the server

`disableExports()` now also disables `b-generate`. The draft comes from the same server as the
export; leaving the button live would offer an action whose only possible outcome is the banner the
user is already reading.

### 3.7 CSS ??the one non-obvious rule

`#toolbar label` is a flex **row** (label left, control right), and a textarea in one would be
squeezed to a slit. `#toolbar label.stacked` opts this single control out, by name ??specificity
(1,1,1) beats (1,0,1), so it wins cleanly rather than by accident of order.

## 4. Tests added (`tests/canvas/test_app.py`) ??17, **not yet run**

Every test is written to survive the endpoint **ceasing to be a mock**. What is under test is the
*contract*: valid `canvas-ir/1`, live SHA, survives the editor's own gate, costs what a model call
would. A real author replaces `mock_ir()` and nothing else ??if that swap breaks one of these, it
broke the contract, not the test.

**The one that matters most is `test_the_generated_deck_EXPORTS`**: it feeds what `/api/generate` said
straight into `/api/export`. That closes the loop through the real validator, the real pin check and
the real renderer, and it is the only assertion here that a merely plausible-looking payload could
not satisfy.

Server side: valid payload 쨌 exports 쨌 live SHA and no literal 쨌 is a diagram 쨌 prompt not read 쨌
costs 1.5 s 쨌 bad request refused immediately 쨌 6 shapes of missing prompt all 422 쨌 shares the body
guard 쨌 writes nothing to disk 쨌 imports no network library (greps **every** import line, including
the lazy `import uvicorn` inside `main()`).

Editor side: prompt and button are in the toolbar and **not** in the property panel (which is hidden
whenever nothing is selected ??exactly the state you write a prompt in) 쨌 posts to `/api/generate` 쨌
hands off to the same gate 쨌 one undo step, pushed by the caller 쨌 a refusal costs no undo step 쨌 the
loading state always clears 쨌 generate dies with the server.

The extractors these lean on (`_js_function`, `_js_code`, `_toolbar`, `_panel`) already exist. I
checked my new JS against their two standing assumptions: **no braces inside any string or comment**
in `generate()` / `setBusy()` (brace-matching would desync), and **no `//` or `/*` inside a string
literal** (comment-stripping would eat code). Both hold.

```js
   * loadIR() actually accepted the payload. loadIR() must not push for itself ??it is lifted out by
   * name and executed in Node against a stubbed stage, where snapshot() does not exist.
   */
  async function generate() {
    if (!CONTEXT) return;   // the server is unreachable and the button is already disabled

    var prompt = $('p-prompt').value.trim();
    if (!prompt) {
      setStatus('Type a prompt first.');
      $('p-prompt').focus();
      return;
    }

    clearWarnings();
    setBusy(true);
    setStatus('Generating??);
    try {
      var res = await fetch('/api/generate', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: prompt }),
      });
      if (!res.ok) {
        var data = {};
        try { data = await res.json(); } catch (e) { /* a non-JSON error body */ }
        warn('Generate failed (HTTP ' + res.status + ')', data.detail || res.statusText);
        setStatus('Generate failed.');
        return;
      }

      var ir = await res.json();
      var before = snapshot();
      try {
        loadIR(ir);        // the SAME gate the file import goes through: it judges, then it commits
        pushUndo(before);  // it took: replacing the whole deck is ONE step, and it is reversible
        setStatus('Generated ' + (ir.elements || []).length +
                  ' element(s) ??MOCK payload; no model was called.');
      } catch (e) {
        // The stage is UNCHANGED ??loadIR() judges the whole payload before it touches anything ??
        // and nothing was pushed, so a refused draft costs no undo step either.
        warn('That draft was refused ??the stage is unchanged', String(e.message || e));
        setStatus('Generate refused.');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      warn('Could not reach the server', String(e));
      setStatus('Generate failed.');
    } finally {
      // In a `finally`, because every path above returns from somewhere, and the one thing worse
      // than a slow button is a button that never comes back.
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  /* aria-busy is the STATE; the CSS pulse is only its costume. `disabled` is what actually stops a
   * second POST ??a double press would race two loadIR()s and push two undo steps for one draft. */
  function setBusy(on) {
    var b = $('b-generate');
    b.disabled = on;
    b.setAttribute('aria-busy', String(on));
    $('p-prompt').disabled = on;
  }

  $('b-generate').addEventListener('click', generate);

  /* Ctrl+Z inside the PROMPT is the browser's undo, not ours.
   *
   * The global handler runs undo/redo in FRONT of its editingText() guard on purpose ??so that undo
   * still works with the focus in the size box, which is exactly where the focus is right after the
   * edit you want to undo. This textarea is the one control where that is wrong: the user is typing
   * prose, they expect their keystrokes back, and what they would get instead is their whole deck
   * rolled back. Stop the event here rather than widen the global exception: the exception belongs
   * to this box, not to <input> at large. */
  $('p-prompt').addEventListener('keydown', function (ev) {
    var k = String(ev.key || '').toLowerCase();
    if ((ev.ctrlKey || ev.metaKey) && (k === 'z' || k === 'y')) ev.stopPropagation();
  });
```

And in `disableExports()`:

```js
  function disableExports(why) {
    $('b-export').disabled = true;
    $('b-json').disabled = true;
    // The draft comes from the same server. Leaving it live would offer a button whose only possible
    // outcome is the banner the user is already reading.
    $('b-generate').disabled = true;
    setStatus(why);
  }
```

Gate 1 compliance: no measured-geometry API, no `12700`, no `zIndex`, no `4472C4`, and none of the banned canvas sizes (`1920/1080/1280/720/1440/810`) appear in the added text. `editingText()` already treats `TEXTAREA` as text entry, so the Delete key won't eat a selected element while you type a prompt.

## 1. What Phase 3 is

One endpoint, `POST /api/generate`, and the editor affordance that drives it. It is a **mock**: no
model, no network, no reading of the prompt. It returns one hardcoded `canvas-ir/1` deck, 1.5 s late.

The deliverable is **the seam**, not the author. The editor's request shape, its loading state, its
failure paths and its hand-off to `loadIR()` are all exercised end to end, so that swapping the mock
for a real author is a change to **one function** (`mock_ir()`) and to nothing else.

Two decisions carry the phase, and both are refusals:

**The prompt is not read, and the mock does not pretend to read it.** The brief said "hardcoded
payload", and the tempting embellishment ??echo the prompt into the title so the demo looks alive ??is the one thing that would ruin it. It makes a mock you cannot tell apart from a model, and it
carries author-supplied text (control characters and all) into an IR that `validate.py` then refuses
at *export* time, which is the worst possible place to discover it. `test_the_prompt_is_NOT_read`
posts two different prompts and asserts one deck.

**The mock says "MOCK" on the slide itself.** A canned deck that escapes into a real presentation
announces itself, in a footnote textbox. It costs one element and it is the difference between a
demo and an incident.

---

## 2. `src/aippt/canvas/app.py`

### 2.1 The shared body guard ??the reason `api_export` was touched at all

`_read_json(request) -> (payload, error)` now holds the size-and-JSON preamble that `api_export` used
to own inline, and both POST routes call it. This is the only change to an existing code path, and it
is a pure extraction: same two checks, same order, same status codes.

Both size checks survive the move, because both are load-bearing and it is not obvious:

- the **declared** `Content-Length` check refuses a megabyte before we buffer it;
- the **actual** `len(raw)` check exists because a **chunked** body declares no length at all, and
  would otherwise walk straight past the first check.

A second copy of that reasoning in `api_generate` would have been a second thing to forget to update.
`[REDACTED]` pins that the new route inherits both (413 on an
oversized body, 400 on truncated JSON, no traceback in either).

### 2.2 `mock_ir(pin)` ??a pure function of the pin, which is the seam

It takes the pin and returns a deck. **No request, no app state, no I/O.** That signature is the
entire point: a real author replaces this function and touches nothing else, and
`[REDACTED]` calls it directly, with no server in the picture, to
hold that shape.

**The template SHA and the layout index are injected from the live pin, never written as literals.**
A literal SHA would go stale the day the template is re-pinned (Sec 4.3) and would then hand every
user a 409 on a deck they did not author. This is the identical argument that put `/api/context`
there for the editor, and `[REDACTED]` asserts *both* that
the payload carries the live SHA **and that the SHA does not appear in `app.py` at all**.

The deck is three cards and two arrows ??a diagram, not a wall of text, because a payload that does
not exercise the IR proves only that JSON can be posted over HTTP. Checked against `schema.json`:

| element | required by schema | emitted |
|---|---|---|
| `connector` 횞2 | `id, type, kind, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, width, arrow` | all 9, `arrow: "end"` |
| `rect` 횞3 | `id, type, x, y, w, h, fill` | all 7, plus optional `text` |
| `textbox` 횞2 | `id, type, x, y, w, h, fill` | all 7; **`fill: None` is stated, not omitted** |
| `run` | `t, size, color` | all 3; `color` on every run |

`fill` is required *even when null* precisely because omitting it is how a shape silently inherits
theme `accent1` (Office blue). Stating `None` is the schema encoding that invariant, and both
textboxes state it.

Colours are `#FF0032` (brand red, from `style.BRAND_RED`), `#FFFFFF`, `#1A1A1A`, `#6B727C`. No
`#4472C4` anywhere ??that is the banned accent1.

**Array order is z-order**: the two connectors come **first**, so the lines sit *behind* the cards
they join. That is the convention the editor already follows when it inserts one, and
`[REDACTED]` asserts `elements[0]` is a connector.

### 2.3 The geometry clears the reserved regions ??checked by arithmetic, not by eye

From `geometry.py`: `HEADER_RESERVED = (0, 0, 960, 92)`, `FOOTER_RESERVED = (733.6, 500, 960, 540)`,
and `intersects()` is **half-open**, so edge contact is not a collision.

| element | box (x1, y1 ??x2, y2) | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `subtitle` | 60, 132 ??900, 196 | top 132 > 92 ??|
| `flow_1` | 304, 290 ??358, 290 | ??|
| `flow_2` | 602, 290 ??656, 290 | ??|
| cards 횞3 | 60/358/656, 232 ??+244, 348 | rightmost ends at 900 < 914.4 ??|
| `mock_note` | 60, 392 ??900, 436 | bottom 436 < 500 ??|

Nothing touches the header, nothing touches the footer, nothing leaves 960횞540. The arrows leave and
arrive at the cards' vertical centre (`_MID_Y = 232 + 116/2 = 290`), which is derived, not typed.

### 2.4 The mock is validated before it is served

`validate(ir)` runs on the way out, by **the same validator the export path runs**. Nobody eyeballs
this payload, and a mock that failed validation would demonstrate a working pipeline while breaking
the only thing the pipeline carries.

It cannot fail because of anything the caller sent ??so if it fails, **it is our bug: a 500, never a
422.** That distinction is deliberate and it is in the code.

### 2.5 The 1.5 s is spent on the success path only

`MOCK_LATENCY_S = 1.5`, and it is not padding: the editor's loading state is real UI with a real
failure mode (a button you can press twice), and a mock that answered instantly would never exercise
it.

A malformed request is refused **before** the sleep, because no model would have been called for that
one either ??charging the user 1.5 s to be told their body was empty simulates the wrong thing. Two
tests pin it in both directions: the success path must cost ??1.2 s, the 422 must cost < 1.0 s.

---

## 3. The editor (`index.html`, `style.css`, `editor.js`)

### 3.1 It is a mock and the UI says so at rest

A `mock` tag next to the heading, and a hint line under the button: *"No model is called. The server
returns a fixed deck after 1.5 s, and it replaces the stage (Ctrl+Z brings yours back)."* An "AI"
affordance that looks production-ready while returning a canned deck is the one thing this panel must
not be ??and saying so only in the change log means saying it to nobody.

### 3.2 `generate()` does not validate, and that is the design

It POSTs, then hands what comes back **straight to `loadIR()`**. There is no second judge here.

`loadIR()` is the one door into the stage: it judges every element *before* it clears anything, and
it refuses the whole deck if one element is illegal. A payload from `/api/generate` is **no more
trusted than a file the user opened** ??today it is a fixed mock, tomorrow it is a model, and a model
is exactly the author most likely to put a box on the Vieworks logo. A second copy of the judge in
`generate()` would be a second source of truth, and the first thing to drift.
`[REDACTED]` asserts `loadIR(ir)` is
called and that `illegalReason` is **not** mentioned.

### 3.3 One draft is one undo step, and the caller pushes it

`snapshot()` / `pushUndo(before)` straddle the `loadIR()` call, lifted from the file-import path for
the same reason it lives there:

- Generate **replaces the whole deck**. That is one undo step.
- `pushUndo` comes **after** `loadIR()` returns, so a **refused draft costs no undo step** ??nothing
  was pushed, and the stage is untouched. `[REDACTED]` asserts that
  ordering against the *comment-stripped* source, so prose cannot satisfy it.
- `loadIR()` must **not** push for itself: it is lifted out by name and executed in Node against a
  stubbed stage, where `snapshot()` does not exist. Calling it from inside would turn a green rule
  into a `ReferenceError` in the very harness that proves the rule.

### 3.4 The loading state always clears

`setBusy(false)` is in a `finally`, because every path above it returns from somewhere, and the one
thing worse than a slow button is a button that never comes back.

`disabled` is what actually stops a second POST (a double press would race two `loadIR()`s and push
two undo steps for one draft). `aria-busy` is the **state**; the CSS pulse is only its costume, so
what the eye is told, a screen reader is told too.

### 3.5 Ctrl+Z in the prompt box is the browser's, not ours

The global key handler deliberately runs undo/redo **in front of** its `editingText()` guard, so that
undo still works with the focus in the size box ??which is exactly where the focus is right after the
edit you want to undo.

The prompt textarea is the one control where that is wrong: the user is typing prose, expects their
keystrokes back, and would instead get **their whole deck rolled back**. So the textarea stops the
event locally (`stopPropagation`) rather than widening the global exception ??the exception belongs
to this box, not to `<input>` at large.

(`editingText()` already treats `TEXTAREA` as text entry, so `Delete` will not eat a selected element
while you type a prompt. That was already true; I checked rather than assumed.)

### 3.6 Generate dies with the server

`disableExports()` now also disables `b-generate`. The draft comes from the same server as the
export; leaving the button live would offer an action whose only possible outcome is the banner the
user is already reading.

### 3.7 CSS ??the one non-obvious rule

`#toolbar label` is a flex **row** (label left, control right), and a textarea in one would be
squeezed to a slit. `#toolbar label.stacked` opts this single control out, by name ??specificity
(1,1,1) beats (1,0,1), so it wins cleanly rather than by accident of order.

---

## 4. Tests added (`tests/canvas/test_app.py`) ??17, **not yet run**

Every test is written to survive the endpoint **ceasing to be a mock**. What is under test is the
*contract*: valid `canvas-ir/1`, live SHA, survives the editor's own gate, costs what a model call
would. A real author replaces `mock_ir()` and nothing else ??if that swap breaks one of these, it
broke the contract, not the test.

**The one that matters most is `test_the_generated_deck_EXPORTS`**: it feeds what `/api/generate` said
straight into `/api/export`. That closes the loop through the real validator, the real pin check and
the real renderer, and it is the only assertion here that a merely plausible-looking payload could
not satisfy.

Server side: valid payload 쨌 exports 쨌 live SHA and no literal 쨌 is a diagram 쨌 prompt not read 쨌
costs 1.5 s 쨌 bad request refused immediately 쨌 6 shapes of missing prompt all 422 쨌 shares the body
guard 쨌 writes nothing to disk 쨌 imports no network library (greps **every** import line, including
the lazy `import uvicorn` inside `main()`).

Editor side: prompt and button are in the toolbar and **not** in the property panel (which is hidden
whenever nothing is selected ??exactly the state you write a prompt in) 쨌 posts to `/api/generate` 쨌
hands off to the same gate 쨌 one undo step, pushed by the caller 쨌 a refusal costs no undo step 쨌 the
loading state always clears 쨌 generate dies with the server.

The extractors these lean on (`_js_function`, `_js_code`, `_toolbar`, `_panel`) already exist. I
checked my new JS against their two standing assumptions: **no braces inside any string or comment**
in `generate()` / `setBusy()` (brace-matching would desync), and **no `//` or `/*` inside a string
literal** (comment-stripping would eat code). Both hold.

**(e) The new route** ??immediately after `api_export`:

```python
@app.post("/api/generate")
async def api_generate(request: Request) -> Response:
    """{"prompt": "..."} in, canvas-ir/1 out. A MOCK: no model, no network, no prompt.

    The editor hands what comes back straight to loadIR(), which judges every element before it
    touches the stage -- so from the editor's side this endpoint is already indistinguishable from a
    real author. That is the whole deliverable: the seam is proven before there is anything behind it.
    """
    body, err = await _read_json(request)
    if err is not None:
        return err

    prompt = body.get("prompt") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(prompt, str) or not prompt.strip():
        # Refused BEFORE the sleep. No model would have been called for an empty body either, so
        # charging the user 1.5 s to be told so would be simulating the wrong thing.
        return JSONResponse(
            {"error": "validation", "detail": 'the body must be {"prompt": "<non-empty text>"}'},
            status_code=422,
        )

    # Logged BY LENGTH, never by content: this is an unauthenticated local endpoint and the deck text
    # is the user's, not ours.
    log.info("mock generate: %d-char prompt (not read -- no model is called)", len(prompt))

    ir = mock_ir(request.app.state.pin)

    # THE MOCK IS VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS SERVED, by the same validator the export path runs. Nobody
    # eyeballs this payload on its way out, and a mock that failed validation would demonstrate a
    # working pipeline while breaking the only thing the pipeline carries. It cannot fail because of
    # anything the caller sent -- so if it fails, it is OUR bug: a 500, never a 422.
    try:
        validate(ir)
    except CanvasValidationError as exc:
        log.exception("the MOCK payload does not validate -- this is a server bug, not a user error")
        return JSONResponse({"error": "mock", "detail": str(exc)}, status_code=500)

    await asyncio.sleep(MOCK_LATENCY_S)
    return JSONResponse(ir)
```

**(f) The shared body guard** ??next to `_too_large()`:

```python
async def _read_json(request: Request) -> tuple[Any, JSONResponse | None]:
    """The body guard both POST routes share. Returns (payload, None) or (None, error).

    Both size checks are needed and both are here: a chunked body declares no Content-Length, so the
    header check alone can be walked straight past, and the real-length check alone would have us
    buffer a megabyte before objecting to it.
    """
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared is not None and declared.isdigit() and int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return None, _too_large()

    raw = await request.body()
    if len(raw) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:  # chunked bodies declare no length; check the real thing too
        return None, _too_large()

    try:
        return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")), None
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        # str(exc) is json's own "Expecting ',' delimiter: line 3 column 9" -- useful, and it leaks
        # nothing but the shape of the body the caller just sent us.
        return None, JSONResponse(
            {"error": "malformed", "detail": f"body is not valid UTF-8 JSON: {exc}"},
            status_code=400,
        )
```

**(g) The mock author** ??before `main()`:

```python
# --- the mock author (Phase 3) [REDACTED]
#
# Three cards and two arrows, laid out inside BODY_SAFE (45.6, 92 -> 914.4, 500). The numbers are
# stated once, here, so that "why is that card at 656?" has an answer you can read instead of
# arithmetic you have to redo.

_CARD_Y = 232.0
_CARD_W = 244.0
_CARD_H = 116.0
```
