```python
def _card(eid: str, x: float, heading: str, detail: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "id": eid,
        "type": "rect",
        "x": x,
        "y": _CARD_Y,
        "w": _CARD_W,
        "h": _CARD_H,
        "fill": f"#{BRAND_RED}",
        "text": {
            "align": "CENTER",
            "valign": "MIDDLE",
            "paragraphs": [
                {"runs": [{"t": heading, "size": 18, "bold": True, "color": _PAPER}]},
                {"runs": [{"t": detail, "size": 13, "color": _PAPER}]},
            ],
        },
    }


def _arrow(eid: str, x1: float, x2: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "id": eid,
        "type": "connector",
        "kind": "straight",
        "x1": x1,
        "y1": _MID_Y,
        "x2": x2,
        "y2": _MID_Y,
        "color": f"#{BRAND_RED}",
        "width": 2,
        "arrow": "end",
    }


def mock_ir(pin: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The hardcoded deck /api/generate answers with. THE PROMPT IS NOT READ.

    Saying that plainly is the point of the function. A mock that appeared to respond to the prompt
    -- by echoing it into the title, say -- would be a mock you could not tell apart from a model,
    and the first thing it would do is carry author-supplied control characters into an IR that
    validate.py then refuses at export time. The real author replaces THIS FUNCTION and nothing else,
    which is why it takes the pin and returns a deck: no request, no app state, no I/O of its own.

    THE TEMPLATE SHA AND THE LAYOUT INDEX ARE INJECTED FROM THE LIVE PIN, never written as literals.
    A literal SHA here would go stale the day the template is re-pinned (Sec 4.3) and would hand
    every user a 409 on a deck they did not author -- the same argument that put /api/context there.

    ARRAY ORDER IS Z-ORDER: the connectors come FIRST, so the lines sit behind the cards they join.
    That is the convention the editor follows when it inserts one.
    """
    return {
        "schema": "canvas-ir/1",
        "canvas": dict(CANVAS),  # a copy -- a caller must not be able to mutate the module constant
        "target": {
            # Informational only; the server never reads a template path out of a payload.
            "template": pin["renderer_template"]["filename"],
            "template_sha256": pin["renderer_template"]["sha256"],
            "layout_index": pin["layout_signature"]["layout_index"],
        },
        "title": "Q3 Marketing Strategy",
        "elements": [
            _arrow("flow_1", _CARD_X[0] + _CARD_W, _CARD_X[1]),
            _arrow("flow_2", _CARD_X[1] + _CARD_W, _CARD_X[2]),
            {
                "id": "subtitle",
                "type": "textbox",
                "x": 60.0,
                "y": 132.0,
                "w": 840.0,
                "h": 64.0,
                # REQUIRED even when null: an omitted fill is exactly how a shape silently inherits
                # theme accent1.
                "fill": None,
                "text": {
                    "align": "LEFT",
                    "valign": "MIDDLE",
                    "paragraphs": [
                        {"runs": [{"t": "???④퀎 ?쇰꼸 ???몄? ??寃?????꾪솚", "size": 20, "bold": True, "color": _INK}]},
                        {"runs": [{"t": "Where the Q3 spend actually moved the number.", "size": 14, "color": _MUTED}]},
                    ],
                },
            },
            *(_card(*c) for c in _CARDS),
            {
                # A mock deck that escapes into a real presentation says so ON THE SLIDE. This costs
                # one textbox and it is the difference between a demo and an incident.
                "id": "mock_note",
                "type": "textbox",
                "x": 60.0,
                "y": 392.0,
                "w": 840.0,
                "h": 44.0,
                "fill": None,
                "text": {
                    "align": "LEFT",
                    "valign": "MIDDLE",
                    "paragraphs": [
                        {"runs": [{
                            "t": "MOCK ??/api/generate returned a fixed deck. No model was called (Phase 3).",
                            "size": 12,
                            "color": _MUTED,
                        }]}
                    ],
                },
            },
        ],
    }
```

Every coordinate clears `HEADER_RESERVED` (ends y=92; the highest element starts at y=132) and `FOOTER_RESERVED` (starts y=500; the lowest ends at y=436), and the x range 60??00 sits inside `BODY_SAFE`.

## 4. `src/aippt/canvas/static/editor.js`

Insert after the `$('f-load')` handler (i.e. after the file-import block, before `stateFromIR`), and amend `disableExports`:

```js
  /* [REDACTED] the AI draft (Phase 3, MOCK) */

  /* POST the prompt, hand what comes back to loadIR(), and nothing else.
   *
   * THERE IS NO VALIDATION HERE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. loadIR() is the one door into the stage: it
   * judges every element BEFORE it clears anything, and it refuses the whole deck if one element is
   * illegal. A payload from /api/generate is no more trusted than a file the user opened ??today it
   * is a fixed mock, tomorrow it is a model, and a model is exactly the author most likely to put a
   * box on the Vieworks logo. A second copy of the judge here would be a second source of truth, and
   * the first thing to drift.
   *
   * The snapshot/pushUndo pair is lifted from the file-import path for the same reason it lives
   * there: this REPLACES THE WHOLE DECK, that is one undo step, and only the caller knows whether
   * loadIR() actually accepted the payload. loadIR() must not push for itself ??it is lifted out by
   * name and executed in Node against a stubbed stage, where snapshot() does not exist.
   */
  async function generate() {
    if (!CONTEXT) return;   // the server is unreachable and the button is already disabled

    var prompt = $('p-prompt').value.trim();
    if (!prompt) {
      setStatus('Type a prompt first.');
      $('p-prompt').focus();
      return;
    }

    clearWarnings();
    setBusy(true);
    setStatus('Generating??);
    try {
      var res = await fetch('/api/generate', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: prompt }),
      });
      if (!res.ok) {
        var data = {};
        try { data = await res.json(); } catch (e) { /* a non-JSON error body */ }
        warn('Generate failed (HTTP ' + res.status + ')', data.detail || res.statusText);
        setStatus('Generate failed.');
        return;
      }

      var ir = await res.json();
      var before = snapshot();
      try {
        loadIR(ir);        // the SAME gate the file import goes through: it judges, then it commits
        pushUndo(before);  // it took: replacing the whole deck is ONE step, and it is reversible
        setStatus('Generated ' + (ir.elements || []).length +
                  ' element(s) ??MOCK payload; no model was called.');
      } catch (e) {
        // The stage is UNCHANGED ??loadIR() judges the whole payload before it touches anything ??
        // and nothing was pushed, so a refused draft costs no undo step either.
        warn('That draft was refused ??the stage is unchanged', String(e.message || e));
        setStatus('Generate refused.');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      warn('Could not reach the server', String(e));
      setStatus('Generate failed.');
    } finally {
      // In a `finally`, because every path above returns from somewhere, and the one thing worse
      // than a slow button is a button that never comes back.
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  /* aria-busy is the STATE; the CSS pulse is only its costume. `disabled` is what actually stops a
   * second POST ??a double press would race two loadIR()s and push two undo steps for one draft. */
  function setBusy(on) {
    var b = $('b-generate');
    b.disabled = on;
    b.setAttribute('aria-busy', String(on));
    $('p-prompt').disabled = on;
  }

  $('b-generate').addEventListener('click', generate);

  /* Ctrl+Z inside the PROMPT is the browser's undo, not ours.
   *
   * The global handler runs undo/redo in FRONT of its editingText() guard on purpose ??so that undo
   * still works with the focus in the size box, which is exactly where the focus is right after the
   * edit you want to undo. This textarea is the one control where that is wrong: the user is typing
   * prose, they expect their keystrokes back, and what they would get instead is their whole deck
   * rolled back. Stop the event here rather than widen the global exception: the exception belongs
   * to this box, not to <input> at large. */
  $('p-prompt').addEventListener('keydown', function (ev) {
    var k = String(ev.key || '').toLowerCase();
    if ((ev.ctrlKey || ev.metaKey) && (k === 'z' || k === 'y')) ev.stopPropagation();
  });
```

And in `disableExports()`:

```js
  function disableExports(why) {
    $('b-export').disabled = true;
    $('b-json').disabled = true;
    // The draft comes from the same server. Leaving it live would offer a button whose only possible
    // outcome is the banner the user is already reading.
    $('b-generate').disabled = true;
    setStatus(why);
  }
```

Gate 1 compliance: no measured-geometry API, no `12700`, no `zIndex`, no `4472C4`, and none of the banned canvas sizes (`1920/1080/1280/720/1440/810`) appear in the added text. `editingText()` already treats `TEXTAREA` as text entry, so the Delete key won't eat a selected element while you type a prompt.

```python
# PHASE 3 -- /api/generate: THE MOCK AUTHOR, AND THE SEAM A REAL ONE SLOTS INTO

# under test is the CONTRACT: the payload is a valid canvas-ir/1 deck, it carries the LIVE pin's SHA
# rather than a literal, it survives the editor's own gate, and it costs what a model call would.

# (uvicorn is imported inside main()). A grep is crude and it is exactly right: there is no
# legitimate reason for any of these names to appear, and the day one does, this fails.
NETWORK_LIBS = ["httpx", "aiohttp", "openai", "anthropic", "urllib.request", "socket", "requests"]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def generated(client: TestClient) -> dict:
    """ONE call, reused: every assertion below is about the same payload, and it costs 1.5 s."""
    r = client.post("/api/generate", json={"prompt": "Q3 留덉????꾨왂??3?④퀎 ?쇰꼸濡??붿빟?댁쨾"})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def [REDACTED](generated: dict):
    validate(generated)  # the real validator, not a re-implementation of it
    assert generated["schema"] == "canvas-ir/1"
    assert generated["canvas"] == {"w": 960, "h": 540, "unit": "pt"}
    assert generated["target"]["layout_index"] == 3


def test_the_generated_deck_EXPORTS(client: TestClient, generated: dict):
    """The whole point. What the mock author says, the real renderer has to be able to draw."""
    r = client.post("/api/export", json=generated)
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    assert r.headers["content-type"] == PPTX_MIME
```

## Assumptions and caveats

- **Nothing was applied and nothing was run.** `pytest` was never executed (code execution is denied here, as in Phase 0 and Phase 2), so treat every line above as unrun code. The tests I wrote are also unrun.
- **The prompt is deliberately not echoed into the payload.** The brief says "hardcoded payload"; echoing author text into the title would carry control characters into an IR that `validate.py` then rejects at export time, and would make the mock indistinguishable from a real author. I chose the honest mock and put the reasoning in `mock_ir()`'s docstring.
- **The 1.5 s sleep is on the success path only.** A malformed request is refused immediately ??no model would have been called for it. A test pins that behaviour both ways.
- **The mock says "MOCK" on the slide itself** (a footnote textbox), so a canned deck that escapes into a real presentation announces itself.
- **`phase3_change_detail.md` was not written.** Its content is essentially this message; whoever re-runs this with write permission should save it to `tasks/AI_Powered_PPT/phase3_change_detail.md` as the brief's YAML block requires.

## Repair Instructions (from codex-critic)
The reviewer blocked your previous patch with the following feedback:
> `generate_deck` accepts any manifest-valid `layout_id` returned by `fill_slide`; it never verifies it matches `entry["layout_id"]`. This breaks the stage-1 layout decision and can validate content against one layout?셲 budget while rendering it with another?셲.
> Raise `CliWorkerSchemaError` when the returned slide layout differs from the outline entry, so the existing repair loop retries it.

> `generate_deck` promises a bounded repair loop for content-budget failures, but the diff never checks any slide content against the manifest budgets. `_parse_and_validate_slide` only validates IR structure and layout existence, so overflowing content is accepted and never re-prompted. This contradicts the function contract and leaves the primary rendering failure unhandled.

> `generate_deck()` now unconditionally calls `check_budget()`, but `render/fit.py:check_budget` is still `NotImplementedError`. Thus every otherwise-valid filled slide aborts before a `GenerationResult` can be returned; the retry loop cannot handle it.
> `_check_slide_budget()` never checks `slide.title` for the supplied manifest: all its placeholders have BODY budgets and none contain `max_title_chars_cjk`, so `title_ph` remains `None`. This leaves title overflow unvalidated.
> `_check_slide_budget()` only compares each block?셲 total character count to `max_bullets * max_chars_per_bullet`. It misses per-item line rounding: e.g., four 11-character bullets in a 6횞10-character placeholder total 44 and pass, but each wraps to two lines (8 lines total), so it overflows. This bypasses the repair loop despite the manifest?셲 ?쏿 bullet that wraps consumes another slot??rule.

Please implement these fixes in `generate_deck`. You must implement the budget checking logic LOCALLY in `_check_slide_budget` or similar. DO NOT just sum the characters! You must calculate the number of lines each bullet takes by doing `math.ceil(len(bullet) / max_chars_per_bullet)`, and sum those lines to ensure it is `<= max_bullets`. ALSO, make sure you validate `slide.title` properly.

Please implement these functions by replacing their `NotImplementedError` bodies with robust Python code. Use `pathlib` for file reads. Be careful with json schemas and ensure `client.complete_json` handles the output correctly.
  `source_refs`; `layout_id` is a closed `enum` built from the manifest's own
  `masters[].layouts[]`, so an invented layout is rejected by the provider's own
  structured-output mechanism, before `validate_against_manifest` would ever see it).
  Returns `result["slides"]`.
- **`fill_slide(client, outline_entry, manifest, sources, *, repair_note="")`** -- looks
  up `outline_entry["layout_id"]` via a new `_find_layout(manifest, layout_id)`, raising
  plain `CliWorkerError` (not `CliWorkerSchemaError`) if it names a layout that doesn't
  exist at all -- a structural defect no repair prompt can fix, and one the outline
  schema's own `enum` should already make unreachable. Formats that layout's placeholder
  budgets with a new `_format_layout_budget(layout)`, styled after
  `analyze_pptx_master.render_catalog`'s per-placeholder line format (reads the
  manifest's own precomputed `content_budget` fields directly; does not import
  `analyze_pptx_master`). Substitutes all six `{{...}}` placeholders in `prompts/
  20_slide_fill.md` and validates via a new `_slide_schema()` -- `ir/schema.json`'s
  `$defs.slide` (lowercase key) lifted to the document root with the full `$defs` carried
  alongside so its internal `#/$defs/...` refs still resolve against the new root.
  **Signature change:** added a keyword-only `repair_note: str = ""`, not in the original
  stub -- required for `generate_deck`'s repair loop to hand back a specific error at
  `{{REPAIR_NOTE}}`. Default-valued and additive; any call written against the original
  4-positional signature is unaffected.
- **`generate_deck(client, topic, sources, manifest_path, *, max_repairs=2)`** -- loads
  the manifest JSON from `manifest_path`, calls `generate_outline` once, then per outline
  entry runs a bounded loop (`max_repairs + 1` attempts) around `fill_slide`. Each attempt:
  1. `_check_layout_matches_entry(slide_dict, entry)` -- critic fix #1. Raises
     `CliWorkerSchemaError` naming both the outline's and the response's `layout_id` on a
     mismatch. `CliWorkerSchemaError`'s own class docstring (`"the model answered but got
     the shape wrong -- repairable by re-prompting"`) is what justifies catching it in the
     retry loop, and the critic's own instruction says the same thing explicitly.
  2. `_parse_and_validate_slide(slide_dict, manifest)` -- wraps the slide in a throwaway
     one-slide deck and reuses `Deck.from_dict` (structural errors JSON Schema cannot
     express, e.g. a ragged table row) + `Deck.validate_against_manifest` (unknown
     `layout_id`, belt-and-suspenders with step 1, raised as `IRValidationError`).
  3. `_check_slide_budget(parsed, layout)` -- critic fixes #2-#5, implemented **locally**,
     without calling `render.fit.check_budget` (still `NotImplementedError`): checks
     `slide.title` against a title-role placeholder's char cap (with the fallback
     heuristic documented in the function's own docstring, and repeated below since it is
     the least obvious design choice in this patch), and each `slide.blocks[i]` against
     `body_placeholders[i]`'s cap, positionally (`ir/schema.json`'s own documented "blocks
     map onto non-title placeholders in order"), using `math.ceil(len(item) /
     max_chars_per_bullet_cjk)` summed per block -- not a raw character sum -- per critic
     fix #5. Verified against the critic's own numeric example: 4 items of 11 chars each,
     cap 10 chars/line, max 6 lines -> `ceil(11/10) = 2` per item x 4 = 8 lines -> 8 > 6,
     correctly flagged (a raw sum of 44 <= 60 would have passed it).

  On either exception type, the error string becomes the next `repair_note` and the loop
  retries; after `max_repairs` failed attempts it raises `RuntimeError` naming the slide
  id, its layout, and the last error. Returns a `GenerationResult` with the assembled
  `Deck` (title truncated to 120 chars, the schema's cap, since `topic` is unbounded
  caller-supplied text), `attempts` = total `fill_slide` calls across the whole deck,
  `repaired` = True if any slide needed more than one attempt, and `token_usage={}`
  (neither CLI track exposes token accounting, so this is honestly empty, not a stub).

## Design choice: the title-placeholder fallback heuristic

`analyze_pptx_master.content_budget()` only tags a placeholder's budget with
`max_title_chars_cjk` when its `ph_type` is TITLE/CENTER_TITLE/VERTICAL_TITLE. Every
placeholder in `reference/layout_manifest.json` is reported as plain `BODY` (confirmed
directly against the manifest for all 5 layouts, all 9 placeholders), so that tag never
appears for this template and a title-vs-body split has to come from somewhere else.
`_check_slide_budget` uses the layout's first placeholder (manifest order, which is
idx-ascending) as the title's target. This was checked, not assumed: idx-ascending is also
top-to-bottom in every layout that has more than one placeholder in this manifest
(cross-checked each placeholder's `inches.top` against its `idx` directly), and the one
single-placeholder layout (`2_?ъ슜??吏???덉씠?꾩썐`) has nothing else for its one
placeholder to be but the title target. The budget applied to it is its own single-line
character cap (`max_chars_per_bullet_cjk`, since `max_bullets` is 1 for every first
placeholder in this manifest) rather than a fabricated multi-line title cap -- there is
nothing in the manifest to derive a 2-line title cap from for a `BODY`-typed placeholder,
and a placeholder whose own budget already says "one line" should not be treated as
holding more. If `content_budget()` is later extended to tag a real title placeholder
(`max_title_chars_cjk` present), the same code path picks that up automatically -- the
lookup checks `max_title_chars_cjk` first and only falls back to
`max_chars_per_bullet_cjk` when it's absent.

## Design choice: aggregate vs. positional body-budget check

Chose positional (`blocks[i]` vs `body_placeholders[i]`) over summing all body text
against a combined pool, since `ir/schema.json` documents the positional mapping as the
actual renderer contract, and a combined-pool check can miss a single overflowing block
whose overage is masked by another under-using block's slack. Blocks beyond the number of
available body placeholders are not checked (the schema says they fall through to
free-floating shapes with no declared budget) -- not a gap, since there's nothing to check
them against. `code`/`image`/`diagram` blocks are excluded from the per-item line count
entirely (`_block_text_items` returns `[]` for them) -- they are not character-budgeted
the way bullets/paragraphs/tables/steps/cards are (monospace/fixed-width, area, and
Mermaid source respectively), and pretending otherwise would just be a second, wrong
estimate on top of the real geometry work `render/fit.py` still owes.

Both the title and body checks budget against the `_cjk` figures unconditionally, never
`_latin`: `ir/schema.json`'s own `deck.language` doc says a `"mixed"` deck (the default)
budgets against CJK as the pessimistic case, and neither the outline nor the fill stage
carries a per-slide language signal this pipeline could budget against `_latin`
selectively even if it wanted to. Budgeting English content against the Korean cap is
stricter than necessary, never unsafe.
